# Nightly builds + integration-only (gh-1538): the SM pre-merge validation
# (ci.yml dispatched per PR head, #1537) is the single test gate — unit
# shards, analyze, coverage, CRAP/jscpd all run there…

blocks.text:
# Nightly builds + integration-only (gh-1538): the SM pre-merge validation
# (ci.yml dispatched per PR head, #1537) is the single test gate — unit
# shards, analyze, coverage, CRAP/jscpd all run there on every change. This
# workflow keeps only what belongs to nightly by nature:
#   build-release — the release-mode build matrix (all store/desktop
#                   targets; PR legs build --debug only),
#   pty-integration — the integration-tagged suites deliberately excluded
#                   from the pre-commit/PR gates (slow, networked, flakier):
#                   PTY/CLI integration incl. the live `llm` provider suite
#                   with secrets, un-quarantined per gh-1199 (it caught the
#                   #1510 TUI wrap regression unit tests could not see).
# When a scheduled run goes red, the auto-issue job files (or updates) a
# single deduped `nightly-red` issue.
name: Nightly

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 3 * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

# SEC-08 (#796): minimal default — the nightly-red filing job grants
# issues: write (+ actions: read) in its own job-level block.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:

  # PTY/CLI integration (issue #177 follow-up, gh-1538): the ONLY remaining
  # test leg in nightly — integration-tagged suites are deliberately
  # excluded from the pre-commit/PR gates (slow, networked, flakier).
  # mock-endpoint tests need NO secrets and always run; live-provider tests
  # self-skip gracefully without keys (their own `skip:` guards), so the
  # blanket "no keys → skip everything" from the old CI job is gone.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # gh-1005 (2026-09-30): the fa-m5 runner-pick probe is GONE — the on-prem
  # M5 pool is ONE runner (fa-m5-1) reserved for genuinely macOS-only work
  # (cube-kernel-live, release macOS/iOS legs). The PTY/CLI integration leg
  # runs on hosted ubuntu-24.04-arm, mirroring the PR legs in ci.yml.
  # gh-1538: the coverage/duration RATCHETS live in the pre-merge gate now
  # (ci.yml pty-coverage-gate, stricter: ratchet-down + shard budgets +
  # auto-filing) — this leg runs the suites and keeps the json/junit
  # evidence artifacts, it does not re-enforce the thresholds nightly.
  pty-integration:
    name: PTY/CLI integration (nightly-only suites)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    permissions:
      contents: read
    env:
      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
      GOOGLE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_API_KEY }}
      OLLAMA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OLLAMA_API_KEY }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'
      - run: dart pub get
      # gh-1300: compile the AOT bundle ONCE for the whole nightly leg and
      # point the FA_BIN seam at it — same shape as ci.yml's fa-aot-build
      # job (the nightly runs one unsharded job, so the build is in-job).
      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-
      - name: dart build cli (AOT bundle, gh-1300)
        run: |
          dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=fa-local
          version=$(sed -n 's/^version: //p' pubspec.yaml)
          echo "$version" > fa-local/bundle/version.txt
          test -x fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
          ./fa-local/bundle/bin/fah --version
      - name: dart test --tags integration (excluding browser-ext — it owns browser-ext.yml)
        # gh-1199 AC5/AC6: this unsharded leg (with secrets) is the
        # SUPERVISED home of the live (`llm`) suite — and it deliberately
        # does NOT apply the flake quarantine: a quarantined file keeps
        # running here nightly, producing the repeat-run proof its fix PR
        # needs for un-quarantine.
        env:
          # gh-1300 FA_BIN seam: every CLI spawn runs the AOT binary
          # (~1 s) instead of the JIT VM+CFE compile (~30 s on ARM).
          FA_BIN: ${{ github.workspace }}/fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
        run: |
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/integration.json"
      # Issue #928 review: the file-reporter writes the json even on a RED
      # leg — convert + upload must not be chained into the failing step.
      # The RAW dart json is the machine-parseable form the gate itself
      # consumes (one format, both sides): a budget-tightening PR downloads
      # `integration-json` and runs check_test_durations.py --update-baseline
      # on it; junit stays for the human/rebalancer view.
      - name: junit durations (budget-tightening evidence)
        if: always()
        run: >-
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py
          test-results/integration.json
          test-results/junit-integration.xml
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: always()
        with:
          name: integration-json
          path: test-results/integration.json
          retention-days: 14
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: always()
        with:
          name: junit-integration
          path: test-results/junit-integration.xml
          retention-days: 14

  # Issue #280 AC3: nightly RELEASE-mode build matrix. The PR legs in
  # ci.yml build --debug (compile-truth); release-only concerns —
  # tree-shaking, R8/minify, dart2js optimisation, icon stripping — are
  # verified here, plus linux/windows bonus targets (the app does not ship
  # there officially yet, so they stay nightly-only per the card's
  # non-goals). A red leg feeds the deduped nightly-red issue via the
  # auto-issue job below.
  build-release:
    name: Build ${{ matrix.target }} (release)
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - target: macos
            runner: macos-latest
            cmd: flutter build macos --release
          - target: ios
            runner: macos-latest
            cmd: flutter build ios --release --no-codesign
          - target: android
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            cmd: flutter build apk --flavor store --release
          - target: web
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            cmd: flutter build web --release
          - target: linux
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            cmd: flutter build linux --release
          - target: windows
            runner: windows-latest
            cmd: flutter build windows --release
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # Same pinned SDK as the PR build legs and the release path (#281).
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - uses: actions/setup-java@de7274f081f381c8f8158605e0321c36c376e2e6 # v6.0.1
        if: matrix.target == 'android'
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '17'
          cache: 'gradle'

      # Linux desktop toolchain + plugin native deps (gtk3 for the runner,
      # gstreamer for audioplayers_linux).
      - name: Install Linux desktop toolchain
        if: matrix.target == 'linux'
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y clang cmake ninja-build pkg-config \
            libgtk-3-dev liblzma-dev libstdc++-12-dev \
            libgstreamer1.0-dev libgstreamer-plugins-base1.0-dev

blocks.text:
# Live LLM testing: the deterministic gate and the supervised benches

gh-1199 — the merge-blocking Quality gate answers exactly one question:
**did this PR break the code?** It runs exclusively on mock LLMs
(`MockLlmServer` and friends), so a model's mood, drift, or rate limit can
never red a merge. Real-model verification answers a different question —
**does the agent work against real models today?** — and it lives in the
bench harnesses (terminal-bench / harbor / MLS-Bench) run **under
supervision**, never in the PR path.

## The `llm` tag boundary

A test that performs live provider I/O carries `@Tags(['integration',
'llm'])`. Everything integration-tagged without `llm` is mock by
construction and runs in the deterministic gate.

| Where | Live (`llm`) tests | Mock (gate) tests |
| --- | --- | --- |
| per-PR integration shards (`pty-integration-linux`) | excluded — `shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm` at selection, `--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm` at invocation | run |
| `integration-mock` leg (no-key) | excluded (`--exclude-tags llm,...`) | run |
| tag-only provider-smoke job (`v*` tags) | run, with secrets | — |
| `nightly.yml` | run, with secrets (supervised, unsharded) | run |
| bench harnesses (terminal-bench / harbor / MLS) | run under supervision | — |
| your machine (debugging) | `dart test --tags "integration && llm"` | `dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags llm` |

The boundary is enforced, not aspirational:

- `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step on every PR, plus
  `test/scripts/llm_tag_boundary_test.dart` in the regular suite) fails
  when an integration-tagged file looks live — a real provider URL, or a
  credential-key literal with no mock/loopback marker — without the `llm`
  tag. A PR that legitimately adds a live test is blocked until tagged;
  genuinely deterministic files that trip the heuristic are pinned in the
  script's `AUDIT_MOCK` audit list with a justification (reviewed in the
  PR). New live tests can never silently join the gate again.
- `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` is the AC1 red/green
  proof: it runs the exact CI shard-selection invocation and asserts no
  live file is emitted — and that without `--exclude-tag llm` one would
  be.
- `llm`-tagged files stay in the `dart analyze` scope of every PR (they
  are excluded from RUN, never from compile — no dead-code rot), and
  nightly compiles and runs them with secrets.

## Mock-script hygiene (gh-1171)

Scripted mocks serve a fixed queue; incidental LLM traffic (memory
auto-tagging, title/summary calls) used to exhaust it and 500-storm the
test. The contract since gh-1171:

- content-route the scripted conversation on unique markers — background
  noise can then never pop a scripted response;
- pin known noise to a **sticky wildcard** scenario (`sticky: true` +
  `match: "Existing tags:"`) so an extra call re-serves the last response
  forever instead of exhausting into a 500;
- keep the conversation scenarios strict — a matched-but-dry scenario must
  still fail loudly, or a real loop regression goes unnoticed.
  `test/integration/memory_taggen_script_pin_test.dart` REG-pins the
  memory leg's wildcard.

## Flake quarantine (gh-1199 AC6)

A test red in **≥2 distinct-SHA gate runs within 24h** is a proven flake
(the #1171 signature — one SHA flipping green/red is noise, one red run is
a regression). `.github/workflows/flake-watch.yml` (hourly,
`scripts/flake_watch.py`) then:

1. creates/updates a `flake`-labelled issue carrying the failing run links
   and SHAs (E3: the quarantine never swallows a real regression — the
   evidence is attached), and
2. opens a reviewable PR adding the file to
   `scripts/test_quarantine.json`.

The gate legs pipe their targets through `scripts/apply_quarantine.py`, so
a quarantined file leaves the deterministic gate until its fix PR lands.
Granularity is the file (dart test cannot exclude one test inside a file);
the entry's `test` field records the offending test. **Nightly
deliberately does NOT apply the quarantine** — the file keeps running
supervised, producing the 10/10-style repeat-run proof (gh-1199 AC4) the
un-quarantine PR must cite.

## What is NOT here

No live runs in any scheduled PR-path job; no bench-harness changes (they
already run supervised); no reduction in mock coverage — the mock suites
keep every assertion the live ones make, minus the network.

# Nightly builds + integration-only (gh-1538): the SM pre-merge validation
# (ci.yml dispatched per PR head, #1537) is the single test gate — unit
# shards, analyze, coverage, CRAP/jscpd all run there…

blocks.text:
# Nightly builds + integration-only (gh-1538): the SM pre-merge validation
# (ci.yml dispatched per PR head, #1537) is the single test gate — unit
# shards, analyze, coverage, CRAP/jscpd all run there on every change. This
# workflow keeps only what belongs to nightly by nature:
#   build-release — the release-mode build matrix (all store/desktop
#                   targets; PR legs build --debug only),
#   pty-integration — the integration-tagged suites deliberately excluded
#                   from the pre-commit/PR gates (slow, networked, flakier):
#                   PTY/CLI integration incl. the live `llm` provider suite
#                   with secrets, un-quarantined per gh-1199 (it caught the
#                   #1510 TUI wrap regression unit tests could not see).
# When a scheduled run goes red, the auto-issue job files (or updates) a
# single deduped `nightly-red` issue.
name: Nightly

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 3 * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

# SEC-08 (#796): minimal default — the nightly-red filing job grants
# issues: write (+ actions: read) in its own job-level block.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:

  # PTY/CLI integration (issue #177 follow-up, gh-1538): the ONLY remaining
  # test leg in nightly — integration-tagged suites are deliberately
  # excluded from the pre-commit/PR gates (slow, networked, flakier).
  # mock-endpoint tests need NO secrets and always run; live-provider tests
  # self-skip gracefully without keys (their own `skip:` guards), so the
  # blanket "no keys → skip everything" from the old CI job is gone.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # gh-1005 (2026-09-30): the fa-m5 runner-pick probe is GONE — the on-prem
  # M5 pool is ONE runner (fa-m5-1) reserved for genuinely macOS-only work
  # (cube-kernel-live, release macOS/iOS legs). The PTY/CLI integration leg
  # runs on hosted ubuntu-24.04-arm, mirroring the PR legs in ci.yml.
  # gh-1538: the coverage/duration RATCHETS live in the pre-merge gate now
  # (ci.yml pty-coverage-gate, stricter: ratchet-down + shard budgets +
  # auto-filing) — this leg runs the suites and keeps the json/junit
  # evidence artifacts, it does not re-enforce the thresholds nightly.
  pty-integration:
    name: PTY/CLI integration (nightly-only suites)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    permissions:
      contents: read
    env:
      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
      GOOGLE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_API_KEY }}
      OLLAMA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OLLAMA_API_KEY }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'
      - run: dart pub get
      # gh-1300: compile the AOT bundle ONCE for the whole nightly leg and
      # point the FA_BIN seam at it — same shape as ci.yml's fa-aot-build
      # job (the nightly runs one unsharded job, so the build is in-job).
      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-
      - name: dart build cli (AOT bundle, gh-1300)
        run: |
          dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=fa-local
          version=$(sed -n 's/^version: //p' pubspec.yaml)
          echo "$version" > fa-local/bundle/version.txt
          test -x fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
          ./fa-local/bundle/bin/fah --version
      - name: dart test --tags integration (excluding browser-ext — it owns browser-ext.yml)
        # gh-1199 AC5/AC6: this unsharded leg (with secrets) is the
        # SUPERVISED home of the live (`llm`) suite — and it deliberately
        # does NOT apply the flake quarantine: a quarantined file keeps
        # running here nightly, producing the repeat-run proof its fix PR
        # needs for un-quarantine.
        env:
          # gh-1300 FA_BIN seam: every CLI spawn runs the AOT binary
          # (~1 s) instead of the JIT VM+CFE compile (~30 s on ARM).
          FA_BIN: ${{ github.workspace }}/fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
        run: |
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/integration.json"
      # Issue #928 review: the file-reporter writes the json even on a RED
      # leg — convert + upload must not be chained into the failing step.
      # The RAW dart json is the machine-parseable form the gate itself
      # consumes (one format, both sides): a budget-tightening PR downloads
      # `integration-json` and runs check_test_durations.py --update-baseline
      # on it; junit stays for the human/rebalancer view.
      - name: junit durations (budget-tightening evidence)
        if: always()
        run: >-
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py
          test-results/integration.json
          test-results/junit-integration.xml
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: always()
        with:
          name: integration-json
          path: test-results/integration.json
          retention-days: 14
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: always()
        with:
          name: junit-integration
          path: test-results/junit-integration.xml
          retention-days: 14

  # Issue #280 AC3: nightly RELEASE-mode build matrix. The PR legs in
  # ci.yml build --debug (compile-truth); release-only concerns —
  # tree-shaking, R8/minify, dart2js optimisation, icon stripping — are
  # verified here, plus linux/windows bonus targets (the app does not ship
  # there officially yet, so they stay nightly-only per the card's
  # non-goals). A red leg feeds the deduped nightly-red issue via the
  # auto-issue job below.
  build-release:
    name: Build ${{ matrix.target }} (release)
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - target: macos
            runner: macos-latest
            cmd: flutter build macos --release
          - target: ios
            runner: macos-latest
            cmd: flutter build ios --release --no-codesign
          - target: android
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            cmd: flutter build apk --flavor store --release
          - target: web
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            cmd: flutter build web --release
          - target: linux
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            cmd: flutter build linux --release
          - target: windows
            runner: windows-latest
            cmd: flutter build windows --release
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # Same pinned SDK as the PR build legs and the release path (#281).
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - uses: actions/setup-java@de7274f081f381c8f8158605e0321c36c376e2e6 # v6.0.1
        if: matrix.target == 'android'
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '17'
          cache: 'gradle'

      # Linux desktop toolchain + plugin native deps (gtk3 for the runner,
      # gstreamer for audioplayers_linux).
      - name: Install Linux desktop toolchain
        if: matrix.target == 'linux'
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y clang cmake ninja-build pkg-config \
            libgtk-3-dev liblzma-dev libstdc++-12-dev \
            libgstreamer1.0-dev libgstreamer-plugins-base1.0-dev

blocks.text:
# Live LLM testing: the deterministic gate and the supervised benches

gh-1199 — the merge-blocking Quality gate answers exactly one question:
**did this PR break the code?** It runs exclusively on mock LLMs
(`MockLlmServer` and friends), so a model's mood, drift, or rate limit can
never red a merge. Real-model verification answers a different question —
**does the agent work against real models today?** — and it lives in the
bench harnesses (terminal-bench / harbor / MLS-Bench) run **under
supervision**, never in the PR path.

## The `llm` tag boundary

A test that performs live provider I/O carries `@Tags(['integration',
'llm'])`. Everything integration-tagged without `llm` is mock by
construction and runs in the deterministic gate.

| Where | Live (`llm`) tests | Mock (gate) tests |
| --- | --- | --- |
| per-PR integration shards (`pty-integration-linux`) | excluded — `shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm` at selection, `--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm` at invocation | run |
| `integration-mock` leg (no-key) | excluded (`--exclude-tags llm,...`) | run |
| tag-only provider-smoke job (`v*` tags) | run, with secrets | — |
| `nightly.yml` | run, with secrets (supervised, unsharded) | run |
| bench harnesses (terminal-bench / harbor / MLS) | run under supervision | — |
| your machine (debugging) | `dart test --tags "integration && llm"` | `dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags llm` |

The boundary is enforced, not aspirational:

- `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step on every PR, plus
  `test/scripts/llm_tag_boundary_test.dart` in the regular suite) fails
  when an integration-tagged file looks live — a real provider URL, or a
  credential-key literal with no mock/loopback marker — without the `llm`
  tag. A PR that legitimately adds a live test is blocked until tagged;
  genuinely deterministic files that trip the heuristic are pinned in the
  script's `AUDIT_MOCK` audit list with a justification (reviewed in the
  PR). New live tests can never silently join the gate again.
- `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` is the AC1 red/green
  proof: it runs the exact CI shard-selection invocation and asserts no
  live file is emitted — and that without `--exclude-tag llm` one would
  be.
- `llm`-tagged files stay in the `dart analyze` scope of every PR (they
  are excluded from RUN, never from compile — no dead-code rot), and
  nightly compiles and runs them with secrets.

## Mock-script hygiene (gh-1171)

Scripted mocks serve a fixed queue; incidental LLM traffic (memory
auto-tagging, title/summary calls) used to exhaust it and 500-storm the
test. The contract since gh-1171:

- content-route the scripted conversation on unique markers — background
  noise can then never pop a scripted response;
- pin known noise to a **sticky wildcard** scenario (`sticky: true` +
  `match: "Existing tags:"`) so an extra call re-serves the last response
  forever instead of exhausting into a 500;
- keep the conversation scenarios strict — a matched-but-dry scenario must
  still fail loudly, or a real loop regression goes unnoticed.
  `test/integration/memory_taggen_script_pin_test.dart` REG-pins the
  memory leg's wildcard.

## Flake quarantine (gh-1199 AC6)

A test red in **≥2 distinct-SHA gate runs within 24h** is a proven flake
(the #1171 signature — one SHA flipping green/red is noise, one red run is
a regression). `.github/workflows/flake-watch.yml` (hourly,
`scripts/flake_watch.py`) then:

1. creates/updates a `flake`-labelled issue carrying the failing run links
   and SHAs (E3: the quarantine never swallows a real regression — the
   evidence is attached), and
2. opens a reviewable PR adding the file to
   `scripts/test_quarantine.json`.

The gate legs pipe their targets through `scripts/apply_quarantine.py`, so
a quarantined file leaves the deterministic gate until its fix PR lands.
Granularity is the file (dart test cannot exclude one test inside a file);
the entry's `test` field records the offending test. **Nightly
deliberately does NOT apply the quarantine** — the file keeps running
supervised, producing the 10/10-style repeat-run proof (gh-1199 AC4) the
un-quarantine PR must cite.

## What is NOT here

No live runs in any scheduled PR-path job; no bench-harness changes (they
already run supervised); no reduction in mock coverage — the mock suites
keep every assertion the live ones make, minus the network.

# Nightly builds + integration-only (gh-1538): the SM pre-merge validation
# (ci.yml dispatched per PR head, #1537) is the single test gate — unit

blocks.text:
# Nightly builds + integration-only (gh-1538): the SM pre-merge validation
# (ci.yml dispatched per PR head, #1537) is the single test gate — unit
# shards, analyze, coverage, CRAP/jscpd all run there on every change. This
# workflow keeps only what belongs to nightly by nature:
#   build-release — the release-mode build matrix (all store/desktop
#                   targets; PR legs build --debug only),
#   pty-integration — the integration-tagged suites deliberately excluded
#                   from the pre-commit/PR gates (slow, networked, flakier):
#                   PTY/CLI integration incl. the live `llm` provider suite
#                   with secrets, un-quarantined per gh-1199 (it caught the
#                   #1510 TUI wrap regression unit tests could not see).
# When a scheduled run goes red, the auto-issue job files (or updates) a
# single deduped `nightly-red` issue.
name: Nightly

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 3 * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

# SEC-08 (#796): minimal default — the nightly-red filing job grants
# issues: write (+ actions: read) in its own job-level block.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:

  # PTY/CLI integration (issue #177 follow-up, gh-1538): the ONLY remaining
  # test leg in nightly — integration-tagged suites are deliberately
  # excluded from the pre-commit/PR gates (slow, networked, flakier).
  # mock-endpoint tests need NO secrets and always run; live-provider tests
  # self-skip gracefully without keys (their own `skip:` guards), so the
  # blanket "no keys → skip everything" from the old CI job is gone.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # gh-1005 (2026-09-30): the fa-m5 runner-pick probe is GONE — the on-prem
  # M5 pool is ONE runner (fa-m5-1) reserved for genuinely macOS-only work
  # (cube-kernel-live, release macOS/iOS legs). The PTY/CLI integration leg
  # runs on hosted ubuntu-24.04-arm, mirroring the PR legs in ci.yml.
  # gh-1538: the coverage/duration RATCHETS live in the pre-merge gate now
  # (ci.yml pty-coverage-gate, stricter: ratchet-down + shard budgets +
  # auto-filing) — this leg runs the suites and keeps the json/junit
  # evidence artifacts, it does not re-enforce the thresholds nightly.
  pty-integration:
    name: PTY/CLI integration (nightly-only suites)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    permissions:
      contents: read
    env:
      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
      GOOGLE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_API_KEY }}
      OLLAMA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OLLAMA_API_KEY }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'
      - run: dart pub get
      # gh-1300: compile the AOT bundle ONCE for the whole nightly leg and
      # point the FA_BIN seam at it — same shape as ci.yml's fa-aot-build
      # job (the nightly runs one unsharded job, so the build is in-job).
      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-
      - name: dart build cli (AOT bundle, gh-1300)
        run: |
          dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=fa-local
          version=$(sed -n 's/^version: //p' pubspec.yaml)
          echo "$version" > fa-local/bundle/version.txt
          test -x fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
          ./fa-local/bundle/bin/fah --version
      - name: dart test --tags integration (excluding browser-ext — it owns browser-ext.yml)
        # gh-1199 AC5/AC6: this unsharded leg (with secrets) is the
        # SUPERVISED home of the live (`llm`) suite — and it deliberately
        # does NOT apply the flake quarantine: a quarantined file keeps
        # running here nightly, producing the repeat-run proof its fix PR
        # needs for un-quarantine.
        env:
          # gh-1300 FA_BIN seam: every CLI spawn runs the AOT binary
          # (~1 s) instead of the JIT VM+CFE compile (~30 s on ARM).
          FA_BIN: ${{ github.workspace }}/fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
        run: |
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/integration.json"
      # Issue #928 review: the file-reporter writes the json even on a RED
      # leg — convert + upload must not be chained into the failing step.
      # The RAW dart json is the machine-parseable form the gate itself
      # consumes (one format, both sides): a budget-tightening PR downloads
      # `integration-json` and runs check_test_durations.py --update-baseline
      # on it; junit stays for the human/rebalancer view.
      - name: junit durations (budget-tightening evidence)
        if: always()
        run: >-
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py
          test-results/integration.json
          test-results/junit-integration.xml
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: always()
        with:
          name: integration-json
          path: test-results/integration.json
          retention-days: 14
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: always()
        with:
          name: junit-integration
          path: test-results/junit-integration.xml
          retention-days: 14

  # Issue #280 AC3: nightly RELEASE-mode build matrix. The PR legs in
  # ci.yml build --debug (compile-truth); release-only concerns —
  # tree-shaking, R8/minify, dart2js optimisation, icon stripping — are
  # verified here, plus linux/windows bonus targets (the app does not ship
  # there officially yet, so they stay nightly-only per the card's
  # non-goals). A red leg feeds the deduped nightly-red issue via the
  # auto-issue job below.
  build-release:
    name: Build ${{ matrix.target }} (release)
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - target: macos
            runner: macos-latest
            cmd: flutter build macos --release
          - target: ios
            runner: macos-latest
            cmd: flutter build ios --release --no-codesign
          - target: android
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            cmd: flutter build apk --flavor store --release
          - target: web
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            cmd: flutter build web --release
          - target: linux
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            cmd: flutter build linux --release
          - target: windows
            runner: windows-latest
            cmd: flutter build windows --release
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # Same pinned SDK as the PR build legs and the release path (#281).
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - uses: actions/setup-java@de7274f081f381c8f8158605e0321c36c376e2e6 # v6.0.1
        if: matrix.target == 'android'
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '17'
          cache: 'gradle'

      # Linux desktop toolchain + plugin native deps (gtk3 for the runner,
      # gstreamer for audioplayers_linux).
      - name: Install Linux desktop toolchain
        if: matrix.target == 'linux'
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y clang cmake ninja-build pkg-config \
            libgtk-3-dev liblzma-dev libstdc++-12-dev \
            libgstreamer1.0-dev libgstreamer-plugins-base1.0-dev

blocks.text:
# Live LLM testing: the deterministic gate and the supervised benches

gh-1199 — the merge-blocking Quality gate answers exactly one question:
**did this PR break the code?** It runs exclusively on mock LLMs
(`MockLlmServer` and friends), so a model's mood, drift, or rate limit can
never red a merge. Real-model verification answers a different question —
**does the agent work against real models today?** — and it lives in the
bench harnesses (terminal-bench / harbor / MLS-Bench) run **under
supervision**, never in the PR path.

## The `llm` tag boundary

A test that performs live provider I/O carries `@Tags(['integration',
'llm'])`. Everything integration-tagged without `llm` is mock by
construction and runs in the deterministic gate.

| Where | Live (`llm`) tests | Mock (gate) tests |
| --- | --- | --- |
| per-PR integration shards (`pty-integration-linux`) | excluded — `shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm` at selection, `--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm` at invocation | run |
| `integration-mock` leg (no-key) | excluded (`--exclude-tags llm,...`) | run |
| tag-only provider-smoke job (`v*` tags) | run, with secrets | — |
| `nightly.yml` | run, with secrets (supervised, unsharded) | run |
| bench harnesses (terminal-bench / harbor / MLS) | run under supervision | — |
| your machine (debugging) | `dart test --tags "integration && llm"` | `dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags llm` |

The boundary is enforced, not aspirational:

- `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step on every PR, plus
  `test/scripts/llm_tag_boundary_test.dart` in the regular suite) fails
  when an integration-tagged file looks live — a real provider URL, or a
  credential-key literal with no mock/loopback marker — without the `llm`
  tag. A PR that legitimately adds a live test is blocked until tagged;
  genuinely deterministic files that trip the heuristic are pinned in the
  script's `AUDIT_MOCK` audit list with a justification (reviewed in the
  PR). New live tests can never silently join the gate again.
- `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` is the AC1 red/green
  proof: it runs the exact CI shard-selection invocation and asserts no
  live file is emitted — and that without `--exclude-tag llm` one would
  be.
- `llm`-tagged files stay in the `dart analyze` scope of every PR (they
  are excluded from RUN, never from compile — no dead-code rot), and
  nightly compiles and runs them with secrets.

## Mock-script hygiene (gh-1171)

Scripted mocks serve a fixed queue; incidental LLM traffic (memory
auto-tagging, title/summary calls) used to exhaust it and 500-storm the
test. The contract since gh-1171:

- content-route the scripted conversation on unique markers — background
  noise can then never pop a scripted response;
- pin known noise to a **sticky wildcard** scenario (`sticky: true` +
  `match: "Existing tags:"`) so an extra call re-serves the last response
  forever instead of exhausting into a 500;
- keep the conversation scenarios strict — a matched-but-dry scenario must
  still fail loudly, or a real loop regression goes unnoticed.
  `test/integration/memory_taggen_script_pin_test.dart` REG-pins the
  memory leg's wildcard.

## Flake quarantine (gh-1199 AC6)

A test red in **≥2 distinct-SHA gate runs within 24h** is a proven flake
(the #1171 signature — one SHA flipping green/red is noise, one red run is
a regression). `.github/workflows/flake-watch.yml` (hourly,
`scripts/flake_watch.py`) then:

1. creates/updates a `flake`-labelled issue carrying the failing run links
   and SHAs (E3: the quarantine never swallows a real regression — the
   evidence is attached), and
2. opens a reviewable PR adding the file to
   `scripts/test_quarantine.json`.

The gate legs pipe their targets through `scripts/apply_quarantine.py`, so
a quarantined file leaves the deterministic gate until its fix PR lands.
Granularity is the file (dart test cannot exclude one test inside a file);
the entry's `test` field records the offending test. **Nightly
deliberately does NOT apply the quarantine** — the file keeps running
supervised, producing the 10/10-style repeat-run proof (gh-1199 AC4) the
un-quarantine PR must cite.

## What is NOT here

No live runs in any scheduled PR-path job; no bench-harness changes (they
already run supervised); no reduction in mock coverage — the mock suites
keep every assertion the live ones make, minus the network.

# Nightly builds + integration-only (gh-1538): the SM pre-merge validation
# (ci.yml dispatched per PR head, #1537) is the single test gate — unit
# shards, analyze, coverage, CRAP/jscpd all run there…

blocks.text:
# Nightly builds + integration-only (gh-1538): the SM pre-merge validation
# (ci.yml dispatched per PR head, #1537) is the single test gate — unit
# shards, analyze, coverage, CRAP/jscpd all run there on every change. This
# workflow keeps only what belongs to nightly by nature:
#   build-release — the release-mode build matrix (all store/desktop
#                   targets; PR legs build --debug only),
#   pty-integration — the integration-tagged suites deliberately excluded
#                   from the pre-commit/PR gates (slow, networked, flakier):
#                   PTY/CLI integration incl. the live `llm` provider suite
#                   with secrets, un-quarantined per gh-1199 (it caught the
#                   #1510 TUI wrap regression unit tests could not see).
# When a scheduled run goes red, the auto-issue job files (or updates) a
# single deduped `nightly-red` issue.
name: Nightly

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 3 * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

# SEC-08 (#796): minimal default — the nightly-red filing job grants
# issues: write (+ actions: read) in its own job-level block.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:

  # PTY/CLI integration (issue #177 follow-up, gh-1538): the ONLY remaining
  # test leg in nightly — integration-tagged suites are deliberately
  # excluded from the pre-commit/PR gates (slow, networked, flakier).
  # mock-endpoint tests need NO secrets and always run; live-provider tests
  # self-skip gracefully without keys (their own `skip:` guards), so the
  # blanket "no keys → skip everything" from the old CI job is gone.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # gh-1005 (2026-09-30): the fa-m5 runner-pick probe is GONE — the on-prem
  # M5 pool is ONE runner (fa-m5-1) reserved for genuinely macOS-only work
  # (cube-kernel-live, release macOS/iOS legs). The PTY/CLI integration leg
  # runs on hosted ubuntu-24.04-arm, mirroring the PR legs in ci.yml.
  # gh-1538: the coverage/duration RATCHETS live in the pre-merge gate now
  # (ci.yml pty-coverage-gate, stricter: ratchet-down + shard budgets +
  # auto-filing) — this leg runs the suites and keeps the json/junit
  # evidence artifacts, it does not re-enforce the thresholds nightly.
  pty-integration:
    name: PTY/CLI integration (nightly-only suites)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    permissions:
      contents: read
    env:
      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
      GOOGLE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_API_KEY }}
      OLLAMA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OLLAMA_API_KEY }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'
      - run: dart pub get
      # gh-1300: compile the AOT bundle ONCE for the whole nightly leg and
      # point the FA_BIN seam at it — same shape as ci.yml's fa-aot-build
      # job (the nightly runs one unsharded job, so the build is in-job).
      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-
      - name: dart build cli (AOT bundle, gh-1300)
        run: |
          dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=fa-local
          version=$(sed -n 's/^version: //p' pubspec.yaml)
          echo "$version" > fa-local/bundle/version.txt
          test -x fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
          ./fa-local/bundle/bin/fah --version
      - name: dart test --tags integration (excluding browser-ext — it owns browser-ext.yml)
        # gh-1199 AC5/AC6: this unsharded leg (with secrets) is the
        # SUPERVISED home of the live (`llm`) suite — and it deliberately
        # does NOT apply the flake quarantine: a quarantined file keeps
        # running here nightly, producing the repeat-run proof its fix PR
        # needs for un-quarantine.
        env:
          # gh-1300 FA_BIN seam: every CLI spawn runs the AOT binary
          # (~1 s) instead of the JIT VM+CFE compile (~30 s on ARM).
          FA_BIN: ${{ github.workspace }}/fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
        run: |
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/integration.json"
      # Issue #928 review: the file-reporter writes the json even on a RED
      # leg — convert + upload must not be chained into the failing step.
      # The RAW dart json is the machine-parseable form the gate itself
      # consumes (one format, both sides): a budget-tightening PR downloads
      # `integration-json` and runs check_test_durations.py --update-baseline
      # on it; junit stays for the human/rebalancer view.
      - name: junit durations (budget-tightening evidence)
        if: always()
        run: >-
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py
          test-results/integration.json
          test-results/junit-integration.xml
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: always()
        with:
          name: integration-json
          path: test-results/integration.json
          retention-days: 14
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: always()
        with:
          name: junit-integration
          path: test-results/junit-integration.xml
          retention-days: 14

  # Issue #280 AC3: nightly RELEASE-mode build matrix. The PR legs in
  # ci.yml build --debug (compile-truth); release-only concerns —
  # tree-shaking, R8/minify, dart2js optimisation, icon stripping — are
  # verified here, plus linux/windows bonus targets (the app does not ship
  # there officially yet, so they stay nightly-only per the card's
  # non-goals). A red leg feeds the deduped nightly-red issue via the
  # auto-issue job below.
  build-release:
    name: Build ${{ matrix.target }} (release)
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - target: macos
            runner: macos-latest
            cmd: flutter build macos --release
          - target: ios
            runner: macos-latest
            cmd: flutter build ios --release --no-codesign
          - target: android
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            cmd: flutter build apk --flavor store --release
          - target: web
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            cmd: flutter build web --release
          - target: linux
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            cmd: flutter build linux --release
          - target: windows
            runner: windows-latest
            cmd: flutter build windows --release
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # Same pinned SDK as the PR build legs and the release path (#281).
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - uses: actions/setup-java@de7274f081f381c8f8158605e0321c36c376e2e6 # v6.0.1
        if: matrix.target == 'android'
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '17'
          cache: 'gradle'

      # Linux desktop toolchain + plugin native deps (gtk3 for the runner,
      # gstreamer for audioplayers_linux).
      - name: Install Linux desktop toolchain
        if: matrix.target == 'linux'
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y clang cmake ninja-build pkg-config \
            libgtk-3-dev liblzma-dev libstdc++-12-dev \
            libgstreamer1.0-dev libgstreamer-plugins-base1.0-dev

# Live LLM testing: the deterministic gate and the supervised benches

gh-1199 — the merge-blocking Quality gate answers exactly one question:
**did this PR break the code?** It runs exclusively on mock LLMs
(`MockLlmServer` and friends), so a model's mood, drift, or rate limit can
never red a merge. Real-model verification answers a different question —
**does the agent work against real models today?** — and it lives in the
bench harnesses (terminal-bench / harbor / MLS-Bench) run **under
supervision**, never in the PR path.

## The `llm` tag boundary

A test that performs live provider I/O carries `@Tags(['integration',
'llm'])`. Everything integration-tagged without `llm` is mock by
construction and runs in the deterministic gate.

| Where | Live (`llm`) tests | Mock (gate) tests |
| --- | --- | --- |
| per-PR integration shards (`pty-integration-linux`) | excluded — `shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm` at selection, `--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm` at invocation | run |
| `integration-mock` leg (no-key) | excluded (`--exclude-tags llm,...`) | run |
| tag-only provider-smoke job (`v*` tags) | run, with secrets | — |
| `nightly.yml` | run, with secrets (supervised, unsharded) | run |
| bench harnesses (terminal-bench / harbor / MLS) | run under supervision | — |
| your machine (debugging) | `dart test --tags "integration && llm"` | `dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags llm` |

The boundary is enforced, not aspirational:

- `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step on every PR, plus
  `test/scripts/llm_tag_boundary_test.dart` in the regular suite) fails
  when an integration-tagged file looks live — a real provider URL, or a
  credential-key literal with no mock/loopback marker — without the `llm`
  tag. A PR that legitimately adds a live test is blocked until tagged;
  genuinely deterministic files that trip the heuristic are pinned in the
  script's `AUDIT_MOCK` audit list with a justification (reviewed in the
  PR). New live tests can never silently join the gate again.
- `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` is the AC1 red/green
  proof: it runs the exact CI shard-selection invocation and asserts no
  live file is emitted — and that without `--exclude-tag llm` one would
  be.
- `llm`-tagged files stay in the `dart analyze` scope of every PR (they
  are excluded from RUN, never from compile — no dead-code rot), and
  nightly compiles and runs them with secrets.

## Mock-script hygiene (gh-1171)

Scripted mocks serve a fixed queue; incidental LLM traffic (memory
auto-tagging, title/summary calls) used to exhaust it and 500-storm the
test. The contract since gh-1171:

- content-route the scripted conversation on unique markers — background
  noise can then never pop a scripted response;
- pin known noise to a **sticky wildcard** scenario (`sticky: true` +
  `match: "Existing tags:"`) so an extra call re-serves the last response
  forever instead of exhausting into a 500;
- keep the conversation scenarios strict — a matched-but-dry scenario must
  still fail loudly, or a real loop regression goes unnoticed.
  `test/integration/memory_taggen_script_pin_test.dart` REG-pins the
  memory leg's wildcard.

## Flake quarantine (gh-1199 AC6)

A test red in **≥2 distinct-SHA gate runs within 24h** is a proven flake
(the #1171 signature — one SHA flipping green/red is noise, one red run is
a regression). `.github/workflows/flake-watch.yml` (hourly,
`scripts/flake_watch.py`) then:

1. creates/updates a `flake`-labelled issue carrying the failing run links
   and SHAs (E3: the quarantine never swallows a real regression — the
   evidence is attached), and
2. opens a reviewable PR adding the file to
   `scripts/test_quarantine.json`.

The gate legs pipe their targets through `scripts/apply_quarantine.py`, so
a quarantined file leaves the deterministic gate until its fix PR lands.
Granularity is the file (dart test cannot exclude one test inside a file);
the entry's `test` field records the offending test. **Nightly
deliberately does NOT apply the quarantine** — the file keeps running
supervised, producing the 10/10-style repeat-run proof (gh-1199 AC4) the
un-quarantine PR must cite.

## What is NOT here

No live runs in any scheduled PR-path job; no bench-harness changes (they
already run supervised); no reduction in mock coverage — the mock suites
keep every assertion the live ones make, minus the network.

# Nightly builds + integration-only (gh-1538): the SM pre-merge validation
# (ci.yml dispatched per PR head, #1537) is the single test gate — unit
# shards, analyze, coverage, CRAP/jscpd all run there…

blocks.text:
# Nightly builds + integration-only (gh-1538): the SM pre-merge validation
# (ci.yml dispatched per PR head, #1537) is the single test gate — unit
# shards, analyze, coverage, CRAP/jscpd all run there on every change. This
# workflow keeps only what belongs to nightly by nature:
#   build-release — the release-mode build matrix (all store/desktop
#                   targets; PR legs build --debug only),
#   pty-integration — the integration-tagged suites deliberately excluded
#                   from the pre-commit/PR gates (slow, networked, flakier):
#                   PTY/CLI integration incl. the live `llm` provider suite
#                   with secrets, un-quarantined per gh-1199 (it caught the
#                   #1510 TUI wrap regression unit tests could not see).
# When a scheduled run goes red, the auto-issue job files (or updates) a
# single deduped `nightly-red` issue.
name: Nightly

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 3 * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

# SEC-08 (#796): minimal default — the nightly-red filing job grants
# issues: write (+ actions: read) in its own job-level block.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:

  # PTY/CLI integration (issue #177 follow-up, gh-1538): the ONLY remaining
  # test leg in nightly — integration-tagged suites are deliberately
  # excluded from the pre-commit/PR gates (slow, networked, flakier).
  # mock-endpoint tests need NO secrets and always run; live-provider tests
  # self-skip gracefully without keys (their own `skip:` guards), so the
  # blanket "no keys → skip everything" from the old CI job is gone.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # gh-1005 (2026-09-30): the fa-m5 runner-pick probe is GONE — the on-prem
  # M5 pool is ONE runner (fa-m5-1) reserved for genuinely macOS-only work
  # (cube-kernel-live, release macOS/iOS legs). The PTY/CLI integration leg
  # runs on hosted ubuntu-24.04-arm, mirroring the PR legs in ci.yml.
  # gh-1538: the coverage/duration RATCHETS live in the pre-merge gate now
  # (ci.yml pty-coverage-gate, stricter: ratchet-down + shard budgets +
  # auto-filing) — this leg runs the suites and keeps the json/junit
  # evidence artifacts, it does not re-enforce the thresholds nightly.
  pty-integration:
    name: PTY/CLI integration (nightly-only suites)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    permissions:
      contents: read
    env:
      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
      GOOGLE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_API_KEY }}
      OLLAMA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OLLAMA_API_KEY }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'
      - run: dart pub get
      # gh-1300: compile the AOT bundle ONCE for the whole nightly leg and
      # point the FA_BIN seam at it — same shape as ci.yml's fa-aot-build
      # job (the nightly runs one unsharded job, so the build is in-job).
      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-
      - name: dart build cli (AOT bundle, gh-1300)
        run: |
          dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=fa-local
          version=$(sed -n 's/^version: //p' pubspec.yaml)
          echo "$version" > fa-local/bundle/version.txt
          test -x fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
          ./fa-local/bundle/bin/fah --version
      - name: dart test --tags integration (excluding browser-ext — it owns browser-ext.yml)
        # gh-1199 AC5/AC6: this unsharded leg (with secrets) is the
        # SUPERVISED home of the live (`llm`) suite — and it deliberately
        # does NOT apply the flake quarantine: a quarantined file keeps
        # running here nightly, producing the repeat-run proof its fix PR
        # needs for un-quarantine.
        env:
          # gh-1300 FA_BIN seam: every CLI spawn runs the AOT binary
          # (~1 s) instead of the JIT VM+CFE compile (~30 s on ARM).
          FA_BIN: ${{ github.workspace }}/fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
        run: |
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/integration.json"
      # Issue #928 review: the file-reporter writes the json even on a RED
      # leg — convert + upload must not be chained into the failing step.
      # The RAW dart json is the machine-parseable form the gate itself
      # consumes (one format, both sides): a budget-tightening PR downloads
      # `integration-json` and runs check_test_durations.py --update-baseline
      # on it; junit stays for the human/rebalancer view.
      - name: junit durations (budget-tightening evidence)
        if: always()
        run: >-
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py
          test-results/integration.json
          test-results/junit-integration.xml
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: always()
        with:
          name: integration-json
          path: test-results/integration.json
          retention-days: 14
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: always()
        with:
          name: junit-integration
          path: test-results/junit-integration.xml
          retention-days: 14

  # Issue #280 AC3: nightly RELEASE-mode build matrix. The PR legs in
  # ci.yml build --debug (compile-truth); release-only concerns —
  # tree-shaking, R8/minify, dart2js optimisation, icon stripping — are
  # verified here, plus linux/windows bonus targets (the app does not ship
  # there officially yet, so they stay nightly-only per the card's
  # non-goals). A red leg feeds the deduped nightly-red issue via the
  # auto-issue job below.
  build-release:
    name: Build ${{ matrix.target }} (release)
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - target: macos
            runner: macos-latest
            cmd: flutter build macos --release
          - target: ios
            runner: macos-latest
            cmd: flutter build ios --release --no-codesign
          - target: android
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            cmd: flutter build apk --flavor store --release
          - target: web
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            cmd: flutter build web --release
          - target: linux
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            cmd: flutter build linux --release
          - target: windows
            runner: windows-latest
            cmd: flutter build windows --release
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # Same pinned SDK as the PR build legs and the release path (#281).
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - uses: actions/setup-java@de7274f081f381c8f8158605e0321c36c376e2e6 # v6.0.1
        if: matrix.target == 'android'
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '17'
          cache: 'gradle'

      # Linux desktop toolchain + plugin native deps (gtk3 for the runner,
      # gstreamer for audioplayers_linux).
      - name: Install Linux desktop toolchain
        if: matrix.target == 'linux'
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y clang cmake ninja-build pkg-config \
            libgtk-3-dev liblzma-dev libstdc++-12-dev \
            libgstreamer1.0-dev libgstreamer-plugins-base1.0-dev

blocks.text:
# Live LLM testing: the deterministic gate and the supervised benches

gh-1199 — the merge-blocking Quality gate answers exactly one question:
**did this PR break the code?** It runs exclusively on mock LLMs
(`MockLlmServer` and friends), so a model's mood, drift, or rate limit can
never red a merge. Real-model verification answers a different question —
**does the agent work against real models today?** — and it lives in the
bench harnesses (terminal-bench / harbor / MLS-Bench) run **under
supervision**, never in the PR path.

## The `llm` tag boundary

A test that performs live provider I/O carries `@Tags(['integration',
'llm'])`. Everything integration-tagged without `llm` is mock by
construction and runs in the deterministic gate.

| Where | Live (`llm`) tests | Mock (gate) tests |
| --- | --- | --- |
| per-PR integration shards (`pty-integration-linux`) | excluded — `shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm` at selection, `--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm` at invocation | run |
| `integration-mock` leg (no-key) | excluded (`--exclude-tags llm,...`) | run |
| tag-only provider-smoke job (`v*` tags) | run, with secrets | — |
| `nightly.yml` | run, with secrets (supervised, unsharded) | run |
| bench harnesses (terminal-bench / harbor / MLS) | run under supervision | — |
| your machine (debugging) | `dart test --tags "integration && llm"` | `dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags llm` |

The boundary is enforced, not aspirational:

- `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step on every PR, plus
  `test/scripts/llm_tag_boundary_test.dart` in the regular suite) fails
  when an integration-tagged file looks live — a real provider URL, or a
  credential-key literal with no mock/loopback marker — without the `llm`
  tag. A PR that legitimately adds a live test is blocked until tagged;
  genuinely deterministic files that trip the heuristic are pinned in the
  script's `AUDIT_MOCK` audit list with a justification (reviewed in the
  PR). New live tests can never silently join the gate again.
- `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` is the AC1 red/green
  proof: it runs the exact CI shard-selection invocation and asserts no
  live file is emitted — and that without `--exclude-tag llm` one would
  be.
- `llm`-tagged files stay in the `dart analyze` scope of every PR (they
  are excluded from RUN, never from compile — no dead-code rot), and
  nightly compiles and runs them with secrets.

## Mock-script hygiene (gh-1171)

Scripted mocks serve a fixed queue; incidental LLM traffic (memory
auto-tagging, title/summary calls) used to exhaust it and 500-storm the
test. The contract since gh-1171:

- content-route the scripted conversation on unique markers — background
  noise can then never pop a scripted response;
- pin known noise to a **sticky wildcard** scenario (`sticky: true` +
  `match: "Existing tags:"`) so an extra call re-serves the last response
  forever instead of exhausting into a 500;
- keep the conversation scenarios strict — a matched-but-dry scenario must
  still fail loudly, or a real loop regression goes unnoticed.
  `test/integration/memory_taggen_script_pin_test.dart` REG-pins the
  memory leg's wildcard.

## Flake quarantine (gh-1199 AC6)

A test red in **≥2 distinct-SHA gate runs within 24h** is a proven flake
(the #1171 signature — one SHA flipping green/red is noise, one red run is
a regression). `.github/workflows/flake-watch.yml` (hourly,
`scripts/flake_watch.py`) then:

1. creates/updates a `flake`-labelled issue carrying the failing run links
   and SHAs (E3: the quarantine never swallows a real regression — the
   evidence is attached), and
2. opens a reviewable PR adding the file to
   `scripts/test_quarantine.json`.

The gate legs pipe their targets through `scripts/apply_quarantine.py`, so
a quarantined file leaves the deterministic gate until its fix PR lands.
Granularity is the file (dart test cannot exclude one test inside a file);
the entry's `test` field records the offending test. **Nightly
deliberately does NOT apply the quarantine** — the file keeps running
supervised, producing the 10/10-style repeat-run proof (gh-1199 AC4) the
un-quarantine PR must cite.

## What is NOT here

No live runs in any scheduled PR-path job; no bench-harness changes (they
already run supervised); no reduction in mock coverage — the mock suites
keep every assertion the live ones make, minus the network.

# Nightly builds + integration-only (gh-1538): the SM pre-merge validation
# (ci.yml dispatched per PR head, #1537) is the single test gate — unit
# shards, analyze, coverage, CRAP/jscpd all run there…

blocks.text:
# Nightly builds + integration-only (gh-1538): the SM pre-merge validation
# (ci.yml dispatched per PR head, #1537) is the single test gate — unit
# shards, analyze, coverage, CRAP/jscpd all run there on every change. This
# workflow keeps only what belongs to nightly by nature:
#   build-release — the release-mode build matrix (all store/desktop
#                   targets; PR legs build --debug only),
#   pty-integration — the integration-tagged suites deliberately excluded
#                   from the pre-commit/PR gates (slow, networked, flakier):
#                   PTY/CLI integration incl. the live `llm` provider suite
#                   with secrets, un-quarantined per gh-1199 (it caught the
#                   #1510 TUI wrap regression unit tests could not see).
# When a scheduled run goes red, the auto-issue job files (or updates) a
# single deduped `nightly-red` issue.
name: Nightly

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 3 * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

# SEC-08 (#796): minimal default — the nightly-red filing job grants
# issues: write (+ actions: read) in its own job-level block.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:

  # PTY/CLI integration (issue #177 follow-up, gh-1538): the ONLY remaining
  # test leg in nightly — integration-tagged suites are deliberately
  # excluded from the pre-commit/PR gates (slow, networked, flakier).
  # mock-endpoint tests need NO secrets and always run; live-provider tests
  # self-skip gracefully without keys (their own `skip:` guards), so the
  # blanket "no keys → skip everything" from the old CI job is gone.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # gh-1005 (2026-09-30): the fa-m5 runner-pick probe is GONE — the on-prem
  # M5 pool is ONE runner (fa-m5-1) reserved for genuinely macOS-only work
  # (cube-kernel-live, release macOS/iOS legs). The PTY/CLI integration leg
  # runs on hosted ubuntu-24.04-arm, mirroring the PR legs in ci.yml.
  # gh-1538: the coverage/duration RATCHETS live in the pre-merge gate now
  # (ci.yml pty-coverage-gate, stricter: ratchet-down + shard budgets +
  # auto-filing) — this leg runs the suites and keeps the json/junit
  # evidence artifacts, it does not re-enforce the thresholds nightly.
  pty-integration:
    name: PTY/CLI integration (nightly-only suites)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    permissions:
      contents: read
    env:
      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
      GOOGLE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_API_KEY }}
      OLLAMA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OLLAMA_API_KEY }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'
      - run: dart pub get
      # gh-1300: compile the AOT bundle ONCE for the whole nightly leg and
      # point the FA_BIN seam at it — same shape as ci.yml's fa-aot-build
      # job (the nightly runs one unsharded job, so the build is in-job).
      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-
      - name: dart build cli (AOT bundle, gh-1300)
        run: |
          dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=fa-local
          version=$(sed -n 's/^version: //p' pubspec.yaml)
          echo "$version" > fa-local/bundle/version.txt
          test -x fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
          ./fa-local/bundle/bin/fah --version
      - name: dart test --tags integration (excluding browser-ext — it owns browser-ext.yml)
        # gh-1199 AC5/AC6: this unsharded leg (with secrets) is the
        # SUPERVISED home of the live (`llm`) suite — and it deliberately
        # does NOT apply the flake quarantine: a quarantined file keeps
        # running here nightly, producing the repeat-run proof its fix PR
        # needs for un-quarantine.
        env:
          # gh-1300 FA_BIN seam: every CLI spawn runs the AOT binary
          # (~1 s) instead of the JIT VM+CFE compile (~30 s on ARM).
          FA_BIN: ${{ github.workspace }}/fa-local/bundle/bin/fah
        run: |
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/integration.json"
      # Issue #928 review: the file-reporter writes the json even on a RED
      # leg — convert + upload must not be chained into the failing step.
      # The RAW dart json is the machine-parseable form the gate itself
      # consumes (one format, both sides): a budget-tightening PR downloads
      # `integration-json` and runs check_test_durations.py --update-baseline
      # on it; junit stays for the human/rebalancer view.
      - name: junit durations (budget-tightening evidence)
        if: always()
        run: >-
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py
          test-results/integration.json
          test-results/junit-integration.xml
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: always()
        with:
          name: integration-json
          path: test-results/integration.json
          retention-days: 14
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: always()
        with:
          name: junit-integration
          path: test-results/junit-integration.xml
          retention-days: 14

  # Issue #280 AC3: nightly RELEASE-mode build matrix. The PR legs in
  # ci.yml build --debug (compile-truth); release-only concerns —
  # tree-shaking, R8/minify, dart2js optimisation, icon stripping — are
  # verified here, plus linux/windows bonus targets (the app does not ship
  # there officially yet, so they stay nightly-only per the card's
  # non-goals). A red leg feeds the deduped nightly-red issue via the
  # auto-issue job below.
  build-release:
    name: Build ${{ matrix.target }} (release)
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - target: macos
            runner: macos-latest
            cmd: flutter build macos --release
          - target: ios
            runner: macos-latest
            cmd: flutter build ios --release --no-codesign
          - target: android
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            cmd: flutter build apk --flavor store --release
          - target: web
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            cmd: flutter build web --release
          - target: linux
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            cmd: flutter build linux --release
          - target: windows
            runner: windows-latest
            cmd: flutter build windows --release
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # Same pinned SDK as the PR build legs and the release path (#281).
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - uses: actions/setup-java@de7274f081f381c8f8158605e0321c36c376e2e6 # v6.0.1
        if: matrix.target == 'android'
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '17'
          cache: 'gradle'

      # Linux desktop toolchain + plugin native deps (gtk3 for the runner,
      # gstreamer for audioplayers_linux).
      - name: Install Linux desktop toolchain
        if: matrix.target == 'linux'
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y clang cmake ninja-build pkg-config \
            libgtk-3-dev liblzma-dev libstdc++-12-dev \
            libgstreamer1.0-dev libgstreamer-plugins-base1.0-dev

blocks.text:
# Live LLM testing: the deterministic gate and the supervised benches

gh-1199 — the merge-blocking Quality gate answers exactly one question:
**did this PR break the code?** It runs exclusively on mock LLMs
(`MockLlmServer` and friends), so a model's mood, drift, or rate limit can
never red a merge. Real-model verification answers a different question —
**does the agent work against real models today?** — and it lives in the
bench harnesses (terminal-bench / harbor / MLS-Bench) run **under
supervision**, never in the PR path.

## The `llm` tag boundary

A test that performs live provider I/O carries `@Tags(['integration',
'llm'])`. Everything integration-tagged without `llm` is mock by
construction and runs in the deterministic gate.

| Where | Live (`llm`) tests | Mock (gate) tests |
| --- | --- | --- |
| per-PR integration shards (`pty-integration-linux`) | excluded — `shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm` at selection, `--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm` at invocation | run |
| `integration-mock` leg (no-key) | excluded (`--exclude-tags llm,...`) | run |
| tag-only provider-smoke job (`v*` tags) | run, with secrets | — |
| `nightly.yml` | run, with secrets (supervised, unsharded) | run |
| bench harnesses (terminal-bench / harbor / MLS) | run under supervision | — |
| your machine (debugging) | `dart test --tags "integration && llm"` | `dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags llm` |

The boundary is enforced, not aspirational:

- `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step on every PR, plus
  `test/scripts/llm_tag_boundary_test.dart` in the regular suite) fails
  when an integration-tagged file looks live — a real provider URL, or a
  credential-key literal with no mock/loopback marker — without the `llm`
  tag. A PR that legitimately adds a live test is blocked until tagged;
  genuinely deterministic files that trip the heuristic are pinned in the
  script's `AUDIT_MOCK` audit list with a justification (reviewed in the
  PR). New live tests can never silently join the gate again.
- `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` is the AC1 red/green
  proof: it runs the exact CI shard-selection invocation and asserts no
  live file is emitted — and that without `--exclude-tag llm` one would
  be.
- `llm`-tagged files stay in the `dart analyze` scope of every PR (they
  are excluded from RUN, never from compile — no dead-code rot), and
  nightly compiles and runs them with secrets.

## Mock-script hygiene (gh-1171)

Scripted mocks serve a fixed queue; incidental LLM traffic (memory
auto-tagging, title/summary calls) used to exhaust it and 500-storm the
test. The contract since gh-1171:

- content-route the scripted conversation on unique markers — background
  noise can then never pop a scripted response;
- pin known noise to a **sticky wildcard** scenario (`sticky: true` +
  `match: "Existing tags:"`) so an extra call re-serves the last response
  forever instead of exhausting into a 500;
- keep the conversation scenarios strict — a matched-but-dry scenario must
  still fail loudly, or a real loop regression goes unnoticed.
  `test/integration/memory_taggen_script_pin_test.dart` REG-pins the
  memory leg's wildcard.

## Flake quarantine (gh-1199 AC6)

A test red in **≥2 distinct-SHA gate runs within 24h** is a proven flake
(the #1171 signature — one SHA flipping green/red is noise, one red run is
a regression). `.github/workflows/flake-watch.yml` (hourly,
`scripts/flake_watch.py`) then:

1. creates/updates a `flake`-labelled issue carrying the failing run links
   and SHAs (E3: the quarantine never swallows a real regression — the
   evidence is attached), and
2. opens a reviewable PR adding the file to
   `scripts/test_quarantine.json`.

The gate legs pipe their targets through `scripts/apply_quarantine.py`, so
a quarantined file leaves the deterministic gate until its fix PR lands.
Granularity is the file (dart test cannot exclude one test inside a file);
the entry's `test` field records the offending test. **Nightly
deliberately does NOT apply the quarantine** — the file keeps running
supervised, producing the 10/10-style repeat-run proof (gh-1199 AC4) the
un-quarantine PR must cite.

## What is NOT here

No live runs in any scheduled PR-path job; no bench-harness changes (they
already run supervised); no reduction in mock coverage — the mock suites
keep every assertion the live ones make, minus the network.
